Abstract
Residential outdoor landscapes constitute the most frequently encountered visual environment for urban residents, yet systematic evaluation of their aesthetic quality and ecological service value remains lacking. This study developed an integrated three-stage framework combining deep learning semantic segmentation, the Scenic Beauty Estimation method, and machine learning regression modeling to assess public visual aesthetic preference for residential outdoor landscapes, understood as one measurable component of the cultural ecosystem services provided by urban residential green spaces. Abstract

Abstract
In China, driven by policies that promote the concentrated and contiguous preservation of traditional villages, the concept of regional and holistic conservation has gained broad acceptance among academia and practitioners. As heritage-preserving entities, traditional villages can be conceptualized as populations sharing and embodying traditional Chinese culture. This study adopts a population-ecology perspective, analyzing 413 traditional villages in Jiangxi Province, to examine village clustering patterns and population relationships, identify traditional village clusters, and propose cluster-based conservation measures. Ripley’s K function, kernel density analysis, entropy analysis, gravity models, and hierarchical nearest-neighbor clustering were employed to examine village clustering patterns and population relationships.
